title: From a drop of fluid to resurrection
translation: Let the human being consider what he was created from: a gushing fluid, coming out from between the backbone and the breastbones. Surely He is able to bring him back, on the day when secrets are laid bare.
body: Ibn Kathir reads verse 8 as resurrection: **whoever began a creation can repeat it**. Citing Ibn ʿAbbas, he takes the **man’s backbone and the woman’s breastbones**: the child comes from both. Job 10 marvels at being formed in the womb; Luther’s **First Article**: “God has made me… body and soul.”
question: Verse 5 points people to their own origin. Why might one’s own birth be offered as evidence for being raised again?
source_label: Ibn Kathir on 86:5-10 · Luther, Small Catechism
reading: Nicolai Sinai, The Qur’an: A Historical-Critical Introduction (2017)
